Legacy campaign

The Price of Power (1982–2001)

Imported power is part of the plan. When regional supply tightens, your company needs both electricity and cash to fall back on.

Explore the Legacy campaign↗ See what’s at stake ↓

Build one utility across nine generations. This chapter is part of that journey.

Location
A fictional California utility
Starts in
1982
Generation
20 years

The situation

Your starting point

The sixth generation inherits a century of utility decisions. This term runs from 1982 through 2001, with a regional import constraint near its end.

You need a cash buffer during the energy crisis as well as enough supply to serve customers. A strategy that works in ordinary trading conditions may leave too little flexibility when the region is short of power.

The choices

What will you do?

  1. 01

    Know your reliance on imports

    Check the contribution of northern supply during the hours that matter. Prepare for the published constraint before it takes effect.

  2. 02

    Keep money available

    Plan for the cash-reserve checkpoint as you choose projects. Useful equipment cannot substitute for money needed to cover operating costs.

  3. 03

    Balance reserve with customer bills

    Compare local backup, connections and spending against affordability and debt limits. The company has to survive the crisis and the next handover.

Put your plan to the test

Bring your inherited company through a term when access to power can no longer be taken for granted.

Open the campaign setup to begin, or continue your existing company. Later generations inherit the choices you made before them.
